title: Properties that past escalations propose for the next intent (a2dlc propose --from-escalations, written to --out, never into the repo)
description: schema_version 1. a2dlc propose --from-escalations reads the counterexamples of earlier runs of the same repo (.a2dlc/escalations.json and .a2dlc/run/*/escalations.json) and turns each one into a property that the next intent could carry: for the arguments of the counterexample the function keeps returning what the base returned. It calls no role. Nothing here is approved: a person (or a signed pre-authorization) decides what goes into the intent; the command never edits an intent. hash is sha256 of target, args and old (each followed by a NUL byte, args and old as the engine wrote them): the same counterexample found by check and by run is one proposal, and a hash already in .a2dlc/reports/proposals.jsonl is not proposed again. probe is the slice-contract probe of that case (kind example, input the arguments, expected the base's result); it has no file or expr, so Tier 0 does not run it until someone writes the assertion in the engine's language. skipped lists what was read and left out, with the reason.

file.description: The file of the target: where the property belongs.
